mainTopic: Badly formed miscarriages: when the mother is טמאה לידה, and the two-backed creature
overview: This amud deals with miscarried fetuses that are badly formed, and asks when the mother still counts as having given birth (טומאת לידה). First, רבי זכאי, רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן argue how much of the lower body must be missing: up to the knee, the orifices, or the navel. The גמרא ties the first argument to whether a טרפה can live, and the second to רבי אלעזר's rule about an animal whose thigh and its recess were removed. רב פפא adds that if anything at all is missing from the head, the mother is טהורה, and רבי יוחנן's rulings about a sealed skull and a palm-branch shape fit this. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a fetus with a mashed or flat face, and רב פפי reworks their argument after a challenge from a ברייתא. A story about רבי חייא's sons teaches that a 'strict' ruling can lead to a leniency, because it gives the woman ימי טוהר. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about a creature with two backs and two spines: whether it can live, whether it counts as a birth, and whether it may be eaten. The גמרא tests their views against two ברייתות. רב's reading of the second ברייתא is given here, and שמואל's reading comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Three opinions on how much of the lower body must be missing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי says up to the knee, רבי ינאי says up to the orifices, and רבי יוחנן (quoting רבי יוסי בן יהושע) says up to the navel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until the knee. רבי ינאי says: until his orifices. רבי יוחנן says in the name of רבי יוסי בן יהושע: until the place of his navel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three opinions on how much of a fetus's lower body must be missing for its mother to be טהורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If enough of the body is missing, the fetus does not count as a real human birth, so the mother does not get טומאת לידה. The three opinions set the cutoff at different points: the knee, the orifices, or the navel. Each one is a bigger missing section than the one before.

keyTerms.meaning: The knee
His orifices (the openings at the bottom of the body)
Navel
Pure; here, the mother is free of טומאת לידה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a 'pure mother' means the fetus is fine. It means the opposite: so much is missing that the fetus does not count as a birth at all.

phrases.english: Until the knee.
Rabbi Yannai says: until his orifices.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua:
Until the place of his navel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אוֹמֵר: עַד לִנְקָבָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of opinions that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cutoff is the knee (רבי זכאי), the orifices (רבי ינאי), or the navel (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: The first two opinions disagree about whether a טרפה can live
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי holds that a טרפה can live, and רבי זכאי holds that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי זכאי and רבי ינאי, the difference is whether a טרפה can live. One Sage holds that a טרפה can live, and the other holds that a טרפה cannot live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the disagreement between רבי זכאי and רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus missing its legs up to the knee is a טרפה. רבי ינאי says a טרפה can survive, so this fetus is still a real birth and the mother is טמאה. רבי זכאי says a טרפה cannot survive, so missing legs up to the knee is already enough to make the mother טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The difference between them is
A creature with a fatal defect
A טרפה can live (survive long-term)

phrases.english: Between Rabbi Zakkai and Rabbi Yannai
the difference between them is whether a tereifa can live.
One Sage holds a tereifa can live,
and the other Sage holds a tereifa cannot live.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין רַבִּי זַכַּאי לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי אִיכָּא בֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first disagreement in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי holds a טרפה can live; רבי זכאי holds it cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that this law about births depends on a basic question in הלכה: whether a טרפה can survive.

steps.title: The second two opinions disagree about רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן disagree about רבי אלעזר's rule that an animal whose thigh and its recess were removed is a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן, the difference is the statement of רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: if the thigh and its recess were removed, the animal is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the disagreement between רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן by pointing to a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a טרפה can live, so that is not what divides them. רבי ינאי agrees with רבי אלעזר: losing the lower body up to the hip area counts as already dead, so missing up to the orifices makes the mother טהורה. רבי יוחנן does not accept this, so he requires more to be missing, up to the navel.

keyTerms.meaning: Thigh (the hind leg)
Its recess (the hollow where the thigh connects)
A carcass, treated as dead even while still moving

phrases.english: Between Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yoḥanan,
the difference between them is the statement of Rabbi Elazar,
as Rabbi Elazar said:
If the thigh and its recess were removed, it is a neveila.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. It means the same thing, just in the feminine form.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין רַבִּי יַנַּאי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אִיכָּא בֵינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second disagreement in step 1, after step 2 explained the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי holds like רבי אלעזר (removing the thigh and its recess means it is already dead); רבי יוחנן does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Knee vs. orifices depends on whether a טרפה can live. Orifices vs. navel depends on רבי אלעזר's rule that removing the thigh and its recess makes it a נבלה.

steps.title: The dispute is only about the lower body; anything missing from the head makes her pure
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the disagreement is only when the lower body is missing. If any amount is missing from the top, the mother is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the dispute is about a fetus missing its body from the bottom up. But if it is missing from the top down, even any small amount, the mother is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets a limit on the dispute: it applies only to a fetus missing its lower body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the opinions above measured from the feet upward. If even a small part is missing from the head, everyone agrees the fetus is not a real birth, so the mother is טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The dispute
From the bottom up
Any amount at all, even a tiny one

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַחְלוֹקֶת מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the dispute is from below to above,
but from above to below,
even any amount, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַחְלוֹקֶת מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the dispute in step 1 to the lower body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If any amount is missing from the head, the mother is טהורה according to all opinions.

steps.title: Support from רבי יוחנן: a fetus with a sealed skull
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רבי יוחנן: a woman who miscarries a fetus whose skull is sealed is טהורה. This supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רב גידל said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a woman who miscarries a fetus whose skull is sealed, its mother is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that matches רב פפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'sealed' skull is a skull that is missing something. Even though it is a defect at the top, רבי יוחנן rules the mother is טהורה. This fits רב פפא's point that a problem in the head makes the mother טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly (introduces support)
A woman who miscarries
His skull is sealed (missing part of the skull)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rav Giddel said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A woman who miscarries a fetus whose skull is sealed,
its mother is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's rule from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that a defect at the top of the body makes the mother טהורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling (via רב גידל) that a fetus with a sealed skull leaves its mother טהורה
steps.whatToRemember: A defect at the top (the head), even a small one, makes the mother טהורה. The three opinions only argue about how much of the lower body must be missing.

steps.title: A fetus shaped like a palm tree's branching top
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes another ruling of רבי יוחנן: if the miscarried fetus looks like the branching top of a palm tree, the mother is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב גידל said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a woman miscarries something shaped like the branching part of a palm tree, its mother is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second ruling from the same chain, רב גידל quoting רבי יוחנן, about another oddly shaped fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower part of this fetus has no form, and its limbs spread out from the top like palm branches. רבי יוחנן rules that this shape is not counted as a real birth, so the mother does not become טמאה לידה. Like the sealed-skull case in step 5, it is another example of a fetus that is too deformed to count as a child.

keyTerms.meaning: the spot where a palm tree's branches spread out
a woman who miscarries
its mother is pure (no טומאת לידה)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A woman who miscarries something like the branching part of a palm tree
phrases.notes: Picture a fetus with a shapeless lower body and arms and legs coming out of the top, like palm branches.

phrases.english: its mother is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain as step 5, about another deformed shape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A palm-branch-shaped fetus does not make the mother טמאה.

steps.title: Dispute over a fetus with a mashed face
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a fetus with a mashed face makes the mother טמאה. ריש לקיש says she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a woman miscarries a fetus whose face is mashed, רבי יוחנן says its mother is impure, and ריש לקיש says its mother is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a fetus whose face is smudged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this fetus the features of the face are blurred but not completely gone. The question is whether a damaged face still counts as a human form for טומאת לידה. רבי יוחנן says it counts, and ריש לקיש says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: its face is mashed or smudged (features blurred but still there)
its mother is impure with טומאת לידה

phrases.english: It was stated: a woman who miscarries a fetus whose face is mashed,
Rabbi Yochanan says: its mother is impure,
Reish Lakish says: its mother is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִי שֶׁפָּנָיו מוּסְמָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new deformity case, the face instead of the body or skull.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: mashed face makes the mother טמאה. ריש לקיש: טהורה.

steps.title: Challenge from the shaped hand or foot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא. It only says we don't worry about a sealed body. If a mashed face also left the mother טהורה, the ברייתא should have mentioned it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: if a woman miscarries a shaped hand or a shaped foot, its mother is impure with the impurity of childbirth, and we don't worry that maybe it came from a sealed body. If ריש לקיש were right, the ברייתא should say: 'maybe it came from a sealed body or from one whose face was mashed!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view using a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists only one 'pure' possibility that we don't worry about, and the mashed face is not on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes that a sealed body would make the mother טהורה, so it bothers to say we don't worry about it. If a mashed face also made her טהורה, it would be a second worry worth dismissing. The fact that the ברייתא doesn't mention it suggests a mashed face makes her טמאה, like רבי יוחנן says.

keyTerms.meaning: a shaped hand, with the fingers clearly formed
impure with the impurity of childbirth
a sealed, undeveloped body, which does not count as a birth
we are not concerned about it
if it were so, it should have taught it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
A woman who miscarries a shaped hand or a shaped foot
phrases.notes: Here חתוכה doesn't mean 'cut off.' It means neatly formed, so the fingers or toes can be seen.

phrases.english: its mother is impure with the impurity of childbirth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא מִגּוּף אָטוּם בָּאתָה.
phrases.english: and we are not concerned that perhaps it came from a sealed body.
And if it is so, let it teach:
phrases.notes: 'If it is so' means if ריש לקיש is right that a mashed face leaves the mother pure.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא מִגּוּף אָטוּם אוֹ מִמִּי שֶׁפָּנָיו מוּסְמָסִין!
phrases.english: 'perhaps from a sealed body or from one whose face is mashed'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that a mashed face leaves the mother טהורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only a sealed body as a 'pure' possibility we can ignore. If a mashed face were also 'pure,' it should have been listed too.

steps.title: The argument is really about a flat face, and the sides are reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי says everyone agrees a mashed face makes the mother טמאה. The real argument is about a completely flat face, and the opinions were stated the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: when the face is mashed, everyone agrees she is impure. They argue when the face is completely flat, and the opinions were stated the other way: רבי יוחנן says its mother is pure, and ריש לקיש says its mother is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי answers the challenge by fixing the version of the מחלוקת. He moves it to a different case and switches who holds which side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now nobody says a mashed face is טהורה, so the ברייתא had no reason to mention it, and the challenge falls away. The argument is moved to a face with no features at all. There רבי יוחנן says the mother is טהורה, and ריש לקיש says she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: its face is plastered flat, with no features visible
everyone agrees
it was stated the other way around (the opinions are reversed)

steps.whatToRemember: Mashed face: everyone says the mother is טמאה. Completely flat face: רבי יוחנן says טהורה, and ריש לקיש says טמאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch out: in step 7 רבי יוחנן said טמאה. After רב פפי's answer, רבי יוחנן says טהורה, but only for the flat face. Don't mix up the two versions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא answers a challenge: it moves the argument to a different case and reverses the names.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said: where its face is mashed,
everyone agrees that she is impure;
where they argue is when its face is flat,
phrases.notes: Flat means plastered smooth, with no eyes, nose or mouth showing at all.

phrases.english: and it was stated the opposite way:
Rabbi Yochanan says its mother is pure,
and Reish Lakish says its mother is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: בְּפָנָיו מוּסְמָסִין כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by changing the case and the names from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument to a different case and reversing the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about a mashed face, with רבי יוחנן saying טמאה and ריש לקיש saying טהורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A mashed face is טמאה according to everyone. The argument is about a flat face: רבי יוחנן says טהורה, and ריש לקיש says טמאה.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש challenge רבי יוחנן from the same ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: In רב פפי's version, the opinions are switched, so ריש לקיש should be able to use the same ברייתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let ריש לקיש challenge רבי יוחנן from this ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רב פפי's switched version. Now רבי יוחנן says a flat face is טהורה, so why didn't ריש לקיש attack him with the ברייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רבי יוחנן used the ברייתא against the person who said טהורה: if that were true, the ברייתא should have mentioned this case too. In רב פפי's version, רבי יוחנן is now the one saying טהורה (for a flat face). So the same attack should work against him, this time made by ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him raise an objection (a way of asking why a challenge was not made)
From this (source)

phrases.english: But let Reish Lakish raise an objection
to Rabbi Yochanan from this!
phrases.notes: 'This' means the ברייתא from step 8, which only says not to worry about a sealed body.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹתְבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב פפי's switched version (step 9) by turning step 8's challenge around
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view in רב פפי's version (flat face is טהורה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only a sealed body as not a worry. If a flat face were also טהורה, it should have been listed, so ריש לקיש could attack רבי יוחנן the same way רבי יוחנן attacked him in step 8.

steps.title: A sealed body and a flat face are the same
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש did not challenge, because רבי יוחנן would answer that a flat face is included in a sealed body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבי יוחנן would answer him: a sealed body is the same as one whose face is flat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש stayed quiet. רבי יוחנן had an easy answer ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat face is simply a sealed body (גוף אטום) in the face area, so the ברייתא did not need to list it separately. This answer works for a flat face but not for a mashed face, which is why רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 8 did hold up in the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: He would answer him (give a reply that removes the problem)
This is the same as
A sealed body, with no openings
His face is flat, smoothed over with no features

phrases.english: Because he would answer him:
A sealed body is
phrases.notes: The pattern 'הַיְינוּ X, הַיְינוּ Y' means 'X and Y are the same thing.'

phrases.english: the same as one whose face is flat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּשַׁנִּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Equating two cases: the ברייתא's sealed body already includes a flat face
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's silence about a flat face shows it is not טהורה
steps.terutzMaskana: A flat face counts as a sealed body, so the ברייתא covered it, and רב פפי's version holds

steps.title: רבי חייא's sons ruled a flat-faced fetus impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's sons return from the villages and report that they ruled טמאה on a flat-faced fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא went out to the villages and came back to their father. He asked them: Did any case come to you? They said: A flat-faced fetus came to us, and we ruled that the woman is טמאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case of a flat-faced fetus. This sets up רבי חייא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons treated the woman as someone who gave birth, which makes her טמאה. Since this case was under debate (step 9), they probably wanted to be careful. Their father will now check their reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Villages
A real case brought for a ruling
We declared her impure

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiyya went out to the villages,
they came before their father.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּלוּם בָּא מַעֲשֶׂה לְיֶדְכֶם?
phrases.english: He said to them: Did any case come to your hands?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: פָּנִים טוּחוֹת בָּא לְיָדֵינוּ,
phrases.english: They said to him: A flat face came to our hands,
phrases.notes: He means a woman who miscarried a fetus with a flat face.

phrases.english: and we declared her impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא נְפוּק לְקִרְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case about the flat face discussed in steps 9 to 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sons ruled that a woman who miscarried a flat-faced fetus is טמאה

steps.title: רבי חייא: your strictness led to a leniency
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא tells his sons to reverse their ruling, because calling her a new mother gives her days in which blood is treated as pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go and declare pure what you declared impure. What were you thinking, to be strict? It is a strictness that leads to a leniency, because you gave her ימי טוהר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא overturns his sons' ruling. He shows them that their 'careful' ruling was actually lenient in another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she counts as having given birth, after her days of טומאה she gets ימי טוהר, when blood she sees does not make her impure. If the fetus does not count as a birth, any blood she sees is treated normally and can make her impure. So the ruling of טמאה brings a leniency with it, and רבי חייא rules טהורה, meaning she is not treated as a new mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Your thinking, your reasoning
A strictness that leads to a leniency
Days of purity after a birth, when blood a woman sees does not make her impure

steps.confusionAlert: When רבי חייא says 'declare her pure', he does not mean she is fully free of all impurity. He means she does not get the status of a woman who gave birth, so she also does not get ימי טוהר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches an important rule for deciding cases: before choosing the 'strict' option, check whether it leads to a leniency somewhere else.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וְטַהֲרוּ מָה שֶׁטִּמֵּאתֶם.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go out and declare pure what you declared impure.
What was your thinking, to be strict?
It is a strictness that leads to a leniency,
since you are giving her days of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְאוּ וְטַהֲרוּ מָה שֶׁטִּמֵּאתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חייא responds to and reverses his sons' ruling from step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who miscarries a flat-faced fetus is not treated as a new mother, because ruling טמאה would give her ימי טוהר, which is a leniency

steps.title: A creature with two backs and two spines
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue whether such a creature counts as a birth for a woman and whether it may be eaten when found in an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If a woman or animal miscarries a creature with two backs and two spines, רב says: for a woman it is not a ולד, and for an animal it is forbidden to eat. שמואל says: for a woman it is a ולד, and for an animal it is permitted to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a different unusual shape. רב and שמואל disagree about it for both a woman and an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion stays consistent across both cases. רב treats this creature as not a real offspring, so the woman is not impure from birth, and in an animal it is forbidden. שמואל treats it as a real offspring, so the woman is impure from birth, and in an animal it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature
Two backs
Spines
An offspring, a birth that counts for the laws of a woman who gave birth
Forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: רב: two backs and two spines is not a ולד in a woman and is forbidden in an animal. שמואל: it is a ולד in a woman and is permitted in an animal.

phrases.english: It was stated: One who miscarries a creature

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּים וּשְׁנֵי שִׁדְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: that has two backs and two spines,
Rav says: In a woman, it is not an offspring,
in an animal, it is forbidden to eat.
And Shmuel says: In a woman, it is an offspring,
in an animal, it is permitted to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּפֶּלֶת בְּרִיָּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּים וּשְׁנֵי שִׁדְרָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about another unusual miscarried form
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: not a ולד in a woman and forbidden in an animal. שמואל: a ולד in a woman and permitted in an animal.

steps.title: What exactly are רב and שמואל arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the root of the disagreement between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the real issue is behind the argument of רב and שמואל from the last step. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 we only saw the two rulings. Now the גמרא wants the reason underneath them, so it can show that each ruling comes from a different view of the creature.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root of an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the רב and שמואל argument in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying issue that splits רב and שמואל.

steps.title: The argument is about רב חנין בר אבא's two-backed creature
steps.stepSummary: They disagree about the creature called השסועה, which רב חנין בר אבא explains has two backs and two spines.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about what רב חנין בר אבא said. He said the word 'השסועה' in the פסוק refers to a creature that has two backs and two spines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is connected to a teaching of רב חנין בר אבא. He reads the word השסועה as a separate creature with two backs and two spines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists animals that are not kosher, and רב חנין בר אבא reads השסועה as one more forbidden creature: one with two backs and two spines. Once we know this creature is forbidden, the question becomes where such a creature can actually be found.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the split one'; here it means a creature with two backs and two spines
A creature, a living thing
Backs
Spines

phrases.english: About the teaching of רב חנין בר אבא,
for רב חנין בר אבא said:
"The split one" means a creature

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁנֵי שִׁדְרָאוֹת.
phrases.english: that has two backs and two spines.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְרַב חָנִין בַּר אַבָּא, דְּאָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by naming the source the argument is built on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about the creature השסועה, which has two backs and two spines.

steps.title: Does the two-backed creature really exist?
steps.stepSummary: רב says it never lives in the world, so the ban is about a fetus in its mother. שמואל says it does exist, so the ban is about a living animal, and a fetus like this is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: there is no such living creature in the world. When ה׳ taught it to משה, He taught it about one found inside its mother. שמואל says: there is such a creature in the world. When ה׳ taught it to משה, He taught it about one living in the world, but one inside its mother is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Each side explains what the תורה's ban on the two-backed creature is talking about. רב and שמואל disagree on whether such a creature can live outside the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a two-backed creature cannot survive, so the ban must be about a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal, and that fetus is forbidden. שמואל holds that it can live, so the ban is about a living animal, and a two-backed fetus inside its mother stays permitted. This explains their argument from step 14 about eating such a creature found in an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: In the world, meaning living and walking around outside the womb
He taught it to him
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳
Inside its mother's womb
It is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רב: the creature does not live, so the ban is about a fetus, and that fetus is forbidden. שמואל: the creature does live, so the ban is about a living animal, and a fetus like this is permitted.

phrases.english: רב said: such a creature does not exist in the world,
and when the Merciful One taught it to משה,
He taught it about one in its mother's womb.
And שמואל said: such a creature does exist in the world,
and when the Merciful One taught it to משה,
He taught it about one living in the world,
but one in its mother's womb is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בְּרִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא לֵיתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חנין בר אבא's teaching to explain each side of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a two-backed creature cannot live, so the ban is about a fetus, which is forbidden. שמואל: it can live, so the ban is about a living animal, and the fetus is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests a person with two backs can live
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא brings a ברייתא saying a כהן with two backs and two spines cannot serve, which implies such a person lives. This is hard for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא challenged רב: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says anyone who has two backs and two spines cannot do the Temple service. So such a person does live, and this is difficult for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא attacks רב's claim that a two-backed creature cannot live. He brings a ברייתא about a כהן with two backs and two spines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There would be no point in disqualifying a כהן with two backs from the service unless such a כהן could actually be alive. That suggests two-backed creatures can survive, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit for the Temple service (said of a כהן with a blemish)
So we see; this shows that
That it lives

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב:
phrases.english: רב שימי בר חייא challenged רב:
רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁנֵי שִׁדְרָאוֹת
phrases.english: Anyone who has two backs and two spines
phrases.notes: He is talking about a כהן.

phrases.english: is unfit for the service.
So we see that such a person lives,
and this is difficult for רב!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's position from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that a two-backed creature does not live in the world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule about a כהן with two backs only makes sense if such a person can be alive.

steps.title: רב: the ברייתא means a crooked spine
steps.stepSummary: רב praises the question but explains that the ברייתא is about a person whose spine is crooked, not one with two real spines.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are שימי! It is talking about someone whose spine is crooked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently. The person in the ברייתא only looks like he has two backs because his spine is bent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crooked spine can look like two spines, and that person can live and is disqualified as a blemish. So the ברייתא does not prove that a creature with two real backs can survive, and רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'You are שימי!', praise meaning 'a good question, as I'd expect from you'
Crooked, bent

steps.confusionAlert: "שימי את" is not an insult. It is praise for a sharp question, and then רב gives his answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are שימי!
phrases.notes: He means: a well-asked question, just what I'd expect from you.

phrases.english: It means one whose spine is crooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שִׁימִי אַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי בר חייא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source (it is about a different case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a person with two real backs and spines, so such a creature lives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a crooked spine that only looks like two, so it proves nothing against רב.

steps.title: A ברייתא about forbidden fetuses mentions the two-backed creature
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists fetuses that are forbidden by how early they were born, and then says the creature with two backs and two spines is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Some fetuses are forbidden. A small animal born in its fourth month, or a large animal born in its eighth month, or earlier than that, is forbidden. This excludes one that has two backs and two spines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא as a challenge. It lists fetuses that are forbidden, and at the end it mentions the two-backed creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals born too early, before they could be fully formed, are forbidden. The ברייתא then mentions the creature with two backs and two spines, which seems to treat it as a forbidden fetus. That looks difficult for שמואל, who said such a fetus inside its mother is permitted, and the גמרא will deal with this next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fetuses
Small livestock (sheep and goats)
Large livestock (cattle)
From this point and earlier
This excludes; this leaves out

phrases.english: They challenged: among fetuses there are some that are forbidden:
one born at four months for small livestock,
phrases.notes: Small livestock normally carry for five months, so a four-month birth is too early.

phrases.english: one born at eight months for large livestock,
phrases.notes: Large livestock normally carry for nine months.

phrases.english: and anything earlier than that is forbidden.
This excludes one that has
two backs and two spines.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: יֵשׁ בְּעוּבָּרִין שֶׁהֵן אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's defense, the גמרא raises a new ברייתא that bears on the רב and שמואל argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument in step 17, apparently שמואל's view that a two-backed fetus in its mother is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions the two-backed creature in its list about forbidden fetuses, which seems to say such a fetus is forbidden.

steps.title: What does 'excluded' mean? A challenge to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the point of the ברייתא from step 20. The word 'excluded' seems to mean the two-backed creature is forbidden even as a fetus inside its mother, and that goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'excluded' mean? Doesn't it mean excluded from the group of fetuses, because these are forbidden even while still inside their mothers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out why the ברייתא it quoted is a problem. It reads the word 'excluded' as meaning that this creature is forbidden even while it is still a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal is permitted. If the ברייתא pulls the two-backed creature out of that group, it is forbidden even inside the womb. That clashes with שמואל, who said such a fetus is permitted (step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'went out'. Here it means 'is excluded' from the rule.
From the group of fetuses, meaning the ones that are normally permitted.
Inside their mothers' wombs.

phrases.english: What does "excluded" mean?
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the ברייתא from the previous step, about the creature with two backs and two spines.

phrases.english: Does it not mean excluded from the category of fetuses
since they are forbidden even in their mothers' wombs?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי יָצָא? לָאו יָצָא מִכְּלַל עוּבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge started in step 20 by stating the inference drawn from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that a two-backed fetus inside its mother is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא 'excludes' the two-backed creature from the fetus rule. That suggests it is forbidden even inside the womb, which is the opposite of שמואל's ruling.

steps.title: Each sage reads the ברייתא his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both רב and שמואל can explain the ברייתא in a way that fits their own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב explains it according to his reasoning, and שמואל explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that the ברייתא can be read two ways, and the next steps will show each reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reject the ברייתא. It says the ברייתא's wording is flexible enough for both sides, so it does not prove the case against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains or interprets a source so that it fits.
According to his own line of reasoning.

phrases.english: Rav explains it according to his reasoning
and Shmuel explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וּשְׁמוּאֵל מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by saying the ברייתא can be read to fit each sage.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dual reading of the source: the ברייתא fits both opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא clearly forbids the two-backed fetus inside the womb, against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each sage has a reading of the ברייתא that matches his own view.

steps.title: רב's reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the ברייתא this way: premature animals are forbidden only once they are born, and inside the slaughtered mother they are permitted. The two-backed creature is excluded from that permission, so it is forbidden even inside the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב explains it his way: an animal born in the fourth month for small animals, or the eighth month for large animals, or earlier, is forbidden. When is this said? When it came out into the world. But inside its mother's womb it is permitted. Excluded is one with two backs and two spines, which is forbidden even inside its mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב reads the ברייתא. In his reading, the 'excluded' clause connects to the rule that fetuses inside the womb are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'excluded' means the two-backed creature does not get the usual permission for a fetus found inside its mother, so it is forbidden even there. This is the same reading the challenge in step 21 assumed, and it fits רב's view from step 17 that such a creature never lives and the ban is about a fetus. The real answer for שמואל is his own reading, which comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Small domesticated animals, like sheep and goats.
Large domesticated animals, like cattle.
From this point and earlier, meaning born even sooner.
In what case is this said? It narrows the rule just stated.
The air of the world, meaning actually born.
Permitted.

steps.confusionAlert: The word יָצָא appears twice here with two different meanings. In כְּשֶׁיָּצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם it means 'came out', as in was born. In יָצָא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ it means 'is excluded' from the rule.

phrases.english: Rav explains it according to his reasoning:
one born in the fourth month, for small animals
one born in the eighth month, for large animals
from this stage and earlier, it is forbidden.
In what case are these words said?
When it came out into the air of the world
but in its mother's womb, it is permitted.
Excluded is one that has
two backs and two spines
for even in its mother's womb it is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: בֶּן אַרְבָּעָה לְדַקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two readings announced in step 22, the one that fits רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source according to רב's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Excluded' is an open challenge to שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב's reading, which matches the challenge's assumption, the two-backed creature is excluded from the permission for fetuses found inside the womb, which fits his view that it never lives. שמואל's reading, which answers the challenge against him, comes on the next amud.
